core_obligations: Identify the map F(-1) -> F as the one induced by the section s of O(1) via multiplication on the sheaf, and compute it on D_+(T_0) = Spec(k[x_1,...,x_n]) as multiplication of the finite module M by a_0 + sum a_i x_i after trivializing O(1) by T_0 (proof lines 6510-6528).

Prove injectivity on D_+(T_0) by choosing a_0 + sum a_i x_i outside every associated prime of M: Ass(M) is finite, and for each associated prime p the intersection of p with the hyperplane of linear forms is a proper k-subvector space, so a finite union of proper subspaces is avoided (proof lines 6529-6539).

Repeat the argument on each D_+(T_j) to get a finite family of proper subspaces V_1,...,V_m of Gamma(P^n, O(1)) outside whose union s may be chosen, and use that k is infinite to pick such an s (proof lines 6540-6543).
Show the cokernel of F(-1) -> F is annihilated by the image of s : O(-1) -> O, which is the ideal sheaf of H, and obtain the sheaf G on H with i_*G equal to that cokernel (proof lines 6544-6549).
proof_roadmap: Compute the section-induced map locally on the standard affine chart.
Choose the linear form generically to avoid the associated primes of the module.
Cover all charts and use infiniteness of k to choose one section working everywhere.
Identify the cokernel with the pushforward of a sheaf on the hyperplane.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for any coherent module F on projective n-space over an infinite field, a nonzero section s of O(1) such that multiplication F(-1) -> F is injective with cokernel of the form i_*G for the associated hyperplane i : H -> P^n. The proof first computes the map on D_+(T_0) as multiplication by a_0 + sum a_i x_i on the finite module M, then shows injectivity by choosing that element outside all associated primes of M, which is possible because Ass(M) is finite and each prime cuts out a proper k-subvector space, so a finite union of proper subspaces cannot exhaust the infinite field (proof lines 6513-6543). The final step identifies the cokernel as annihilated by the ideal sheaf of H and descends it to the hyperplane (proof lines 6544-6549). H3: the associated-primes-to-subspaces reduction and the geometric descent of the cokernel are independent research-level moves over an infinite field.
